body: The drama is a movie about two people who are super happy together who were about to get married and one night, one damn confession would change everything. I don't want to spoil anything because I think everyone should see this movie and make their own decision about how they would react if they would find out something about their partner. This made me rethink my own relationship because I thought what would I do if I would find out something like that and I can definitely say I would handle it so different from the way the people did in this movie. It felt sometimes so hard to watch, but it was also very funny and just very honest and very real. The chemistry between Zendaya and Robert Pattinson is remarkable.

The drama might be one of the most uncomfortable and awkward watches, which is a massive compliment.

I went into it thinking the film was going to operate on a "Materialist" level of heartfelt humour. Instead, it surprised me when it took a darker turn, and it worked perfectly.

The awkwardness and discomfort are driven by the impressive performances from Zendaya and Patterson, two actors at the top of their game. Patterson's ability to make me physically cringe is unmatched here.

What the film succeeds at is balancing its humour between genuine laughs and dark humour. It also impressed me through its direction and editing. The use of flashbacks and almost dreamlike sequences works to blur reality, adding another layer that elevates it above other films of a similar genre.

At no point does the film feel stagnant. There are constant moments driven by character decisions that made the audience audibly gasp. It is an uncomfortable and painful ride until the end, and that is a good thing.

"The Drama" doesn't feel like a real movie, and even after just getting out of the theatre, I'm still not convinced it is. As I was watching it, I almost started to convince myself that I was about to wake up at any moment - the movie feels like something I dreamt up after a night of heavy drinking; just surreal. I watched this in a virtually empty auditorium, which is a shame because I really wish I knew how the average audience would react to this - crowd pleasing this is not.

Advertised as a romantic comedy, "The Drama" deals with surprisingly heavy, uncomfortable, and quite honestly, shocking content. In today's day and age especially, I was a bit taken aback at what exactly the movie was about. Nothing inherently disturbing happens in the film, but the subject matter itself is indeed disturbing, and I'm surprised that this idea was greenlit, filmed, and widely released - on Easter Weekend, no less! But now that all of that is out of the way, how is the movie?

Your reaction to the subject matter is going to deeply dictate your opinion on this film. My mother, for example, found it "painful" to watch; while I didn't find this movie painful, I did find it uncomfortable but entertaining. As a fan of both Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, I found a lot to enjoy here - there is a charm to their relationship, and I enjoyed watching how a simple, ordinary, but happy relationship developed. I also found it interesting to watch how a simple, ordinary, and happy relationship can potentially start to deteriorate when you find out something unexpected about your partner. Pattinson and Zendaya have really good chemistry, and it was fun to see their different reactions to the situations they found themselves in - from panic and anxiety to anger and distrust, both actors go through many emotional stages, and it was fascinating to witness.

The movie also had a very unique editing style that I think contributed to its dreamy feeling. Images and sounds would sometimes pop in or out, just like they would in a dream or as you're drifting off to sleep; it was a unique, unexpected decision that made the movie interesting to watch. That said, the movie also felt kind of uneventful in a way that's sort of hard to explain. A lot does happen in this movie in terms of just the wide range of emotions that people experience, but when it comes to things actually happening, not much happens - I hope this makes sense.

I don't know. I just feel weird about this movie. I liked watching it well-enough, but the subject matter is so bizarre that I'm still in shock that this movie even exists. I'm glad I watched it, and I was entertained while I was watching it, but I can't say I'd actively recommend "The Drama."

Excellent bizarre romance by same director as Dream Scenario that movie is much weirder but great too. Robert and Zendaya were remarkable throughout, I even love the other cast. The Drama is very easy to enjoy worthy of high ratings, the stories about worst thing you ever done make everything more interesting and this was so well made!

Loved it. It was a great mix of edginess, craziness, and discomfort, mixed in with humorous moments, irony, and dark humor. Classic A24.

I think Robert Pattinson could win an Oscar for his role. He was so good-especially at the end of the movie with the wedding speech scene, and then the scene when he gets home after that. Just unbelievable acting. Super impressive.

Zendaya was great as well, and while her character didn't get as much spotlight as Pattinson's, she still really crushed her parts.

All the characters are complex. None of them are necessarily right or wrong, good or bad. The film does a great job of showing the hypocrisy of some people's beliefs. Is it worse to do something bad on impulse? Or is it worse to back out of doing something seriously planned that is super heinous?

It also asks: can people change over time? Just because somebody was a bad person or had skeletons in their closet a long time ago, does that make them a bad person now?

It's also a really good exploration of how instability can start eating away at you once you begin questioning what you thought you knew. The directors did such a good job showing how every little action gets overthought because of new information. It begs the question: is ignorance bliss?

The cinematography is fantastic, as always for A24. Costume and makeup were all on point. The setting was very cool-I wish I had the loft the main characters were living in. It's literally a young person's dream apartment.

The editing was superb. It took a second to adjust to the jump cuts and flashbacks, but once you got the hang of the pacing, it really added to the experience and the uneasiness of the whole atmosphere.

10/10. Super creative, philosophical, and well executed.
